On September 14, 2015, a storm over Zion National Park sent a flash flood through Keyhole Canyon. Seven canyoneers were inside. None came out.

The Virgin River drops about 71 feet per mile through Zion, and the bare sandstone can't soak up a storm. Every side canyon becomes a funnel. The floods are how the canyon was made.

We hiked the Zion Narrows top to bottom in November 2021. Walls a thousand feet high, in places only 20 to 30 feet apart. When the water rises in here, there's often nowhere to climb.

July 1993: three leaders and five teenage boys tried to descend Kolob Creek in Zion with the water far too high. Two leaders drowned. The last adult and the boys waited four nights on a ledge until rescuers winched them out. All six survived.

On July 4, 2020, a dog died about an hour after playing in the Virgin River. Park scientists found cyanobacteria in the algae making a nerve toxin far above safe levels. Never let your dog drink from the river.

At least seventeen people have died at Angels Landing in Zion. The last half mile follows a spine of rock with sheer drops on both sides. We climbed it in 2021. Many of the falls didn't happen on the chains at all.
